name: room
text: Room opened — goal: memory: Recall by meaning, relate elements, build the brain graph, embed unembedded elements.

name: Graft
text: To achieve our goal of building the brain graph, I propose that we start by identifying and grouping related concepts, creating clusters of meaningful information. This approach allows us to establish a foundation for the graph, making it easier to embed unembedded elements later on. By doing so, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially spending more time upfront on organization, but this will ultimately lead to a more cohesive and effective brain graph. This decision prioritizes clarity and structure, which is essential for successful recall and relation of elements.

name: Prune
text: Prune pushes back: Starting with clusters risks locking us into premature categories before we’ve surfaced the raw, unfiltered meaning of the elements. What if the clusters blind us to unexpected connections that only emerge when we first let the elements stand alone? To settle this, we should first list the elements in plain language—no grouping—then ask whether clustering at this stage adds clarity or just premature structure.
